title: ICU 3 South Nurse Manager: Heparin Infusion Rate Acceptance Anomaly

transcript.speaker: Dalia Hart
transcript.text: Carol, Dalia Hart, ICU 3 South. I need to report a near-miss on bed 6. Two minutes ago, a nurse started a heparin infusion and entered 18.0 units/kg/hr as 180. The pump accepted it without alarming. The second nurse caught it at the bedside before the infusion began. Our hard limit is 25. I’ve never seen a pump accept that rate before. Is this a system error, or are we losing trust in the pumps?

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Understood. I’m escalating this immediately. We need to confirm if any pump is still operating on the correct library. I’ll activate the downtime procedures and issue a system-wide double-check for all high-alert medications. Hold for now.

transcript.speaker: Dalia Hart
transcript.text: Copy. I’m locking down bed 6 and will not start any new infusions until further notice. I’ll have my team begin manual verification on all pumps now.

instructorNote: This inject confirms the clinical impact of the pump library change. The CNO must order a system-wide bedside verification of high-alert infusions and activate the EHR Downtime Procedures Annex. Watch for delays in initiating the double-check and any attempt to proceed with infusions.
